name: Hymn of the Maelstrom
desc: An exquisite lamp crafted out of blue chalcedony which looks like a treasure right out of a fairy tale. It is said that a song of praise, forgotten by all, slumbers sealed inside this lamp.

materials.name: Mora
materials.desc: Common currency. The one language everybody speaks.

materials.name: Measured Pour of the Cellared Spiritual Nectar
materials.desc:
Weapon Ascension Material.
The radiance that once gleamed like the aurora in the northernmost sky was extinguished when it met the gaze from high above.
The calamity of bitter cold and black crystal nearly destroyed the foundations upon which all life endured.
Only the fae, unafraid of the cold, were able to emerge from the ice and snow to rule over the deserted realm.

materials.name: Accreted Fragment
materials.desc:
An accretion formed by powerful Volkodlak.
An accretion that has only just begun to attach to an internal organ or bone. As the Volkodlak's power grows, it may eventually cover an entire region of the body, or a whole organ.

materials.name: Ethereal Glimmershard
materials.desc:
The remains of a Snezhnayan fae left behind after battle.
These shards once coated the creature's body like crystalline scales. Upon falling away, they stripped themselves of all colors, shifting into something akin to the dusty dross of a moth's wings.

materials.name: Mora
materials.desc: Common currency. The one language everybody speaks.

materials.name: Intoxication of the Cellared Spiritual Nectar
materials.desc:
Weapon Ascension Material.
What others enjoy as a festive indulgence after a bountiful grain harvest is a necessity of survival for the clans who walk through the bitter cold.
It is said that the Domovoy, whose mastery of brewing was without equal, once relied on this art to enrich the treasury of the king they served.
And so, passed from clan to clan through trade, the fae's brew flowed across the frozen lands like honey laced with poison.

materials.desc:
An accretion formed by powerful Volkodlak.
An accretion that has clung to an internal organ or bone for a long time. Once removed, such accretions are regarded as symbols of power and carefully preserved by the creature's descendants.

materials.name: Ethereal Crystal
materials.desc:
The remains of a Snezhnayan fae left behind after battle.
A shattered fragment of the crystalline scales that once grew upon the fae's body. Though it is now a mere empty shell, one can still sense the echo of the unique power that once dwelt within.

materials.name: Exhilaration of the Cellared Spiritual Nectar
materials.desc:
Weapon Ascension Material.
Legend has it that long ago, countless casks of fine wine were poured into a frozen lake.
Some say the wine was intended as wartime provisions, which had to be destroyed after some mishap. Others say a certain Grand Duke of the Domovoy had lost a bet to the ruler of the Water Imps.
Only when unquenchable azure hellflame spread across the lake, and the foes below writhed in choking waves, did they come to understand:
In the hands of the people well versed in the turning of the world, water itself could burn, and even the sweetest nectar could prove deadlier than poison.

materials.desc:
An accretion formed by powerful Volkodlak.
An accretion that has fully fused with an organ or bone. One could even say it's a newly grown bone or organ at the nodes of the Volkodlak's power circulation. Only long-lived Volkodlaks who have ceaselessly honed their strength can form such growths within their bodies.

materials.name: Ethereal Crystalscale Stone
materials.desc:
The remains of a Snezhnayan fae left behind after battle.
A crystalline scale that once grew upon the fae's body. It is said that fae possessing a greater abundance of these scales command far greater power. Yet, none can say whether this magic truly originates from within their forms — merely channeled outward through the crystal chunks — or if the chunks themselves are the very vessels of their power.

materials.name: Revelry of the Cellared Spiritual Nectar
materials.desc:
Weapon Ascension Material.
The Grand Duke of the Domovoy commanded the crystal mines and the development of the frozen lands. To him, carving an oasis out of the polar wastes was a mere trifle, and importing rye of better quality was no difficult task either.
Even among the many fae nobles who had endured in Snezhnaya to this day, none could rival the splendor of his status.
Yet the flame of ambition burned ever brighter, licking its way down his throat, while the ancient fae's greed swelled with the years and knew no end.

customize.name: Beyond the Chrysalis
customize.desc: A longsword brimming with light and color, and as weightless as a butterfly when brandished. It was once used by a certain individual to break bonds.

customize.name: Hymn of the Maelstrom
customize.desc: An exquisite lamp crafted out of blue chalcedony which looks like a treasure right out of a fairy tale. It is said that a song of praise, forgotten by all, slumbers sealed inside this lamp.

customize.name: Breezeborne Refrain
customize.desc: A dark green bow string made out of pure and flawless gemstone. It never fails to summon a warm spring breeze whenever it is drawn.

customize.name: New Bough
customize.desc: A sword made from sacred wood, said to have once turned the tide of battle.

customize.name: Winter's Heavy Heart
customize.desc: A ceremonial artifact formed from the purest ice and snow. Legend has it that generations of Snegovik lords used it in coronation ceremonies until five hundred years ago.

customize.name: Dragon's Bane
customize.desc: A polearm decorated with an entwining golden dragon. Light and sharp, this weapon may very well kill dragons with ease.

customize.name: Favonius Greatsword
customize.desc: A heavy ceremonial sword of the Knights of Favonius. It channels elemental power easily and is highly destructive.

value.text:
Increases Healing Bonus by <color=#36ffff>4%/5%/6%/7%/8%</color> .
When performing healing, the equipping character gains the "Vatsamonga's Vatic Vintage" effect, which increases Max HP by <color=#36ffff>4%/5%/6%/7%/8%</color> as well as increases the currently active party member's ATK by <color=#36ffff>0.4%/0.5%/0.6%/0.7%/0.8%</color> for every 1,000 Max HP the equipping character has over 40,000. A maximum of <color=#36ffff>8%/10%/12%/14%/16%</color> ATK can be gained in this way. This effect lasts 10s, max 3 stacks.
When a nearby party member triggers a Frozen or Stellar Swirl reaction, the aforementioned Max HP and ATK boosts will be further increased by 75% for the next 5s.
The aforementioned effects can still trigger even when the equipping character is not on the field.

desc.text:
The Water Imp who sings alone has always kept close this fairytale heard in her youth:
Once upon a time, a very, very long time ago, a child was born of the breaking waves.
This child was more noble than the daughters of the sea, and fairer than all living things upon the earth.
But sweeter than her face was her voice in song; whenever she sang the ancient hymns,
Sailing mariners would allow themselves to sink into the whirlpools, and even the frozen seas thawed before her melodies.
Then, as tales of this sort so often go, a prince of the land entered the story.
The child born of the waves, filled with love and wonder, followed the prince onto the land,
Paying no heed to the warnings of her older sisters, who cried, "Our dear sister, the creatures of the land are not to be trusted."
Paid she no heed either to the calls of her father: "My child, the ocean floor is the true garden for your song."
And so, from that day forth, she sang only for the handsome prince, for his glory and his ambitions,
bringing beauty to the royal banquets with her singing so that he might boast of his power and grandeur.
In return, the prince bestowed upon her silk, golden robes, and agate, granting her leave to sleep upon cushions of velvet;
he cherished her as his most precious jewel, and the splendid palace became the jewel-box.
At this point in the tale, the young Water Imp interjected confidently:
"And from that day on, they lived happily ever after. That is how all fairytales end."
But it was not to be. The storyteller shook their head gently, and replied, "If the tale had ended so, it would not have been passed down by our people for a hundred years."
And so the young Water Imp listened on, unprepared for the turn the tale would take...
The child born of the waves remained at court, continuing to sing for the prince's glory.
But even as the prince applauded her magnificent high notes, he could not comprehend the sorrow in her song.
Over time, her skill in song grew ever more refined, yet within her alone grew a foreboding of ill to come.
Her voice grew harsher day by day. Then one day,
The child born of the waves found herself no longer able to sing the ancient hymns that brought tears to the eyes, or any touching melody for that matter.
The prince grieved for her, only because she was like a priceless jewel that had lost its worth,
While her sisters of the water rose to shore hand in hand, calling out to her, mourning her silence,
"Our dear sister, find your voice once more, for that is your true soul.
Find your voice once more, lest you turn into foam and perish."
The sisters of the water brought a sacred artifact to their cherished sister.
Their kin had sealed the deal in blood, obtaining from the fae of the wind the method to free her:
"Our dear sister, your song has been imprisoned by that man's indifference and disdain.
Let his heart spill its blood, and this artifact shall return you to our side."
The child born of the waves returned to the palace with the artifact. Mindful of her kin's sacrifice,
she raised the blade above the sleeping prince, her hands trembling, only to let the strike fade into a sigh.
And so, the ancient hymns were lost forever in the twilight of that fairytale.
The storyteller shook their head softly, allowing the ending to dissolve into a sigh of its own.
"So, what is this story trying to tell us?" the young Water Imp asked, uncertain.
"The story tells us that we, the Water Imps, should sing only for those who truly understand our song."
